==English== ===Etymology=== From {{inh|en|enm|tall}}, {{m|enm|talle}}, {{m|enm|tal|t=seemly, becoming, handsome, good-looking, excellent, good, valiant, lively in speech, bold, great, large, big}}, from {{inh|en|ang|*tæl}}, {{m|ang|ġetæl|t=swift, ready, having mastery of}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*talaz|t=submissive, pliable, obedient}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*dol-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*del-|t=to aim, calculate, adjust, reckon}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|tal|t=high, lofty, tall}}, {{cog|ofs|tel|t=swift}}, {{cog|osx|gital|t=quick}}, {{cog|goh|gizal|t=active, agile}}, {{cog|got|𐌿𐌽𐍄𐌰𐌻𐍃|t=indocile, disobedient}}. The ''Oxford English Dictionary'' notes: "The sense development [of ''tall''] is remarkable, but is paralleled more or less by that of other adjectives expressing estimation, such as ''[[buxom]]'', ''[[canny]]'', ''[[clean]]'', ''[[clever]]'', ''[[cunning]]'', ''[[deft]]'', ''[[elegant]]'', ''[[handsome]]'', ''[[pretty]]'', ''[[proper]]''; German {{m|de|klein}}, as compared with English ''[[clean]]'', presents the antithesis to modern ''tall'' as compared to ''tall'' in early Middle English. It has been conjectured that in the sense 'high of stature' it is a different word, adopted from the Welsh ''{{m|cy|tal}}'' in some sense; but the latter is, according to Professor Rhŷs, merely a 16th-century borrowing of the English word (in Owen Pughe's Dictionary erroneously mixed up with the genuine Welsh word {{m|cy|tal||end, brow, forehead}}, with which it has no possible connection.)"''Oxford English Dictionary'' '''T''', p. 57. ===Pronunciation=== * {{a|en|UK}} ** {{IPA|en|/tɔːl/|[tʰoːɫ]|a=RP}} *** {{audio|en|En-uk-tall.ogg|a=RP}} ** {{IPA|en|/toːl/|a=SSB}} ** {{IPA|en|/tɔl/|a=Scotland}} ** {{IPA|en|/taːl/|a=Northumbrian}} * {{a|en|US}} ** {{IPA|en|/tɔl/|a=GA}} ** {{IPA|en|/tɑl/|a=cot-caught}} *** {{audio|en|En-us-tall.ogg|a=US,cot-caught}} * {{IPA|en|/toːl/|a=AU,NZ}} * {{rhymes|en|ɔːl|s=1}} ===Adjective=== {{en-adj|er}} # {{lb|en|literal}} Having a top that is far up (''contrast: ''[[deep]] ('''having a bottom that is far down' '').) ## {{lb|en|of a person or two-footed creature}} Having great [[vertical]] extent (usually reckoned from the bottom of the feet to the very top of the head) when standing. (For instance, somebody with a height of over 6 feet would generally be deemed tall.) ##: {{ant|en|short}} ##: {{ux|en|Being '''tall''' is an advantage in basketball.}} ##: {{ux|en|[[ostrich|Ostrich]]es are the tallest living birds.}} ##* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=5|passage=Then came a maid with hand-bag and shawls, and after her a '''tall''' young lady. She stood for a moment holding her skirt above the grimy steps,{{...}}, and the light of the reflector fell full upon her.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=2000|author={{w|Robert Bingham (writer)|Robert Bingham}}|title=Lightning on the Sun|pageurl=http://books.google.com.au/books?id=7GZPnauKdk4C&q=%22journo%22%7C%22journos%22+-intitle:%22%22+-inauthor:%22%22&dq=%22journo%22%7C%22journos%22+-intitle:%22%22+-inauthor:%22%22&hl=en&sa=X&ei=bDKRT-3XKaP3mAWW0rmBAg&redir_esc=y|page=34 |passage=He′d been packed in with all the other journos, standing out only in that he was '''taller''' than most and didn′t make as much noise.}} ## {{lb|en|of an inanimate thing, such as a building, hill, lamp, etc.}} Having its top a long way up; having a great [[vertical]] (and often greater than [[horizontal]]) extent. ##: {{syn|en|high|q=less common, old-styled}} ##: {{ant|en|low|low-rise|short}} ##: {{ux|en|'''Tall''' trees, at least about 30m high.}} ## {{senseid|en|coffee}}{{lb|en|specialized|chiefly|US|of a cup of coffee}} Smaller than [[grande]], usually 8 ounces (~ 230 ml). ##: {{cot|en|grande|venti}} # {{lb|en|of a story}} Hard to believe, such as a [[tall story]] or a [[tall tale]]. #* {{quote-journal|en|year=1870|journal=The Cornhill Magazine|volume=21|page=9 |passage="That's '''tall''' talk."
